invariants: The existing Inventory and Stock Location modules remain the only domain owners.
Store ownership is immutable and cannot be accepted from public input.
SKU and inventory-level uniqueness are scoped to one Store.
Inventory items, levels, reservations, locations, and addresses are filtered before pagination and aggregation.
Reservation quantity changes remain atomic with their owned inventory level.
Product-Inventory, Inventory-Location, and Fulfillment-Location links validate both Store-owned endpoints.
A shared request without verified Store context fails closed in services and PostgreSQL.
Dedicated placement works without request Store input and rejects mismatched context.
No Inventory or Stock Location background path exists in the pinned source; future paths require explicit Store restoration.
Shared production remains disabled until every Phase 7 resource group and admission gate is complete.

implementationSlices.name: schema, persistence, RLS, upgrade and rollback
links, Query, events and background inventory

attackMatrix.proof: Shared operations without Store context are denied.
Client-supplied store_id is overwritten.
Foreign inventory items cannot be read, updated, or deleted.
Foreign stock locations cannot be read, updated, or deleted.
The same SKU can exist in different Stores.
A duplicate SKU in one Store is denied.
An inventory level cannot reference a foreign inventory item.
A reservation cannot reference a foreign inventory item or level.
A stock location cannot reference a foreign address.
Owner reassignment is denied by immutable-owner triggers.
RLS denies direct SQL without transaction Store context.
Aggregate quantities ignore foreign Store rows.
Reservation adjustments change only the owned inventory level.
Product-to-Inventory links reject a foreign endpoint.
Inventory-to-Location hydration rejects a foreign endpoint.
Fulfillment-to-Location links reject a foreign endpoint.
Sales Channel links remain unavailable until Sales Channel certification.
Inventory level create and batch workflows validate owned locations.
Inventory level update workflows validate owned locations.
Query and pagination use module-scoped filters.
Concurrent Store operations cannot rebind one transaction.
Dedicated placement derives and binds its configured Store.
Generated additive migrations backfill legacy rows to dedicated ownership.
Rollback refuses unsafe collapse of Store-scoped SKUs.
